primer.title: Box, Rc and Cow
body: `Box<T>` puts a value on the heap behind a pointer of known size. That is what makes recursive types possible: a `List` that contains a `List` has no finite size, a `List` that contains a `Box<List>` does.
`Rc<T>` is shared ownership: `Rc::clone` does not copy the value, it adds an owner and bumps a counter. The value is dropped when the last owner goes.
`Cow` (clone on write) starts out borrowing. `to_mut()` clones the data the first time a write is needed — and never, if no write happens.

exercises.prompt: This does not compile. What does the compiler object to?

options.text: E0072: `List` is a recursive type with infinite size
options.rationale: A `Cons` holds a `List`, which may hold a `List`… so no size can be computed. `Cons(i32, Box<List>)` stores a fixed-size pointer instead.

options.text: E0277: `Debug` cannot be derived for a recursive type
options.rationale: Deriving `Debug` for recursive types is fine, once the type itself is valid.
That is what the `Box` version prints. As written, the compiler cannot lay the type out in memory.
`Nil` is a variant of `List`, so it has type `List`.
Owners: `sun`, mercury, venus = 3. Venus goes, earth comes = 3. Then the `sun` handle itself is dropped = 2. Every handle reports the same count.
The original `sun` binding is an owner too, not just the planets.
`drop(sun)` removes one owner. The `Sun` value lives on, because mercury and earth still hold it.

options.text: It does not compile: `mercury.sun` is used after `drop(sun)`
options.rationale: `drop(sun)` only gives up *that* handle. `mercury.sun` is another owner of the same value.
`a` never needed a write, so it still borrows. `b` was cloned by the first `to_mut()`; the change went into the clone, and `dirty` is untouched.
`to_mut()` is only reached for negative values. `clean` has none, so no clone is made.
`b` only held a shared borrow of `dirty`. Writing required a private copy; the original cannot change.
`to_mut()` on a borrowed `Cow` clones the data, switches it to `Owned`, and returns `&mut` to the clone.
